title: Just a couple dudes with a lot of sleepless nights working on our Strategy RPG. Really incredible what AI can make possible for gaming!
author: Droochainz
selftext:
We're a 2-man team, 2 buddies from across the world (NYC and Australia) who have known each other for 15+ years.. And we've been working many sleepless nights to create our upcoming game Rise of the Fenarii.

We landed on the idea of creating a Tower Defense originally, but overtime our obsessions have turned the game into something (that we feel) is unique. He's brought a lot of worldbuilding and storytelling into the mix, and I've always had an obsession with innovative gameplay mechanics (specifically boss fights).   
  
As time went on in our development… We started to realize how often the 'Tower Defense' genre tends to lack in both of those things, and we leaned into that even harder.

Here's the link to our Steam page. We'd love your thoughts and a wishlist ;)

[*https://store.steampowered.com/app/5240520/Rise\_of\_the\_Fenarii/*](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5240520/Rise_of_the_Fenarii/)

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body:
I think AI slop as in 1 - it’s very generic AI image rendering and animation that most LLMs produce constantly and very bad. You can’t sit her and see the animation is good ?  That you would buy it? Maybe it is a very good game core loop concept whatever but do you really want to invest so much time and dedication only because you couldn’t fix the art/animations ?

I’ll give you a tip how I keep consistent art animation and style

Ask your LLM to create a art style bible guide. And make sure you tell it that if anything isn’t consistent don’t render it or even implement it into your game but to show you a picture.

Other ways for good art/smooth animations video to spritesheets

Or if you wanna save time so many websites and tools

Look into pixel lab , sprite lab , sprite cook

replies.author: TheLuckyOrangutan
replies.body: So it's an interesting one for us; we wanted to focus on mechanics and world-building mostly, then see how the art pass lands. The UI was a design choice. When we gave it to our 40 playtesters, we had a lot of people really enjoy the gameplay loop; the feedback was mostly about balancing, which we have since worked on. Thanks for the feedback, though. Might take another pass at the UI if it seems off-putting.

replies.author: ntjhtnbr
replies.body: Play testers already got the game. They can't really judge art and UI from selling point of view because they don't need to pay for the game. A real person that you expect to make a choice to pay for this game will see AI slop art and will judge that since no effort was made to appeal to him visually, he can't risk his money no matter how impressive they game might be mechanically.

comments.author: Friend135
comments.body: The trailer doesn’t really do a great job of selling or explaining the hook of the game.  It looks like a vaguely interesting high fantasy tower defense game.  But, why should I play/buy it?  The art is also not very poignant - it doesn’t really “pop” for the audience if that makes sense.  Lastly, the music is very forgettable and doesn’t really match the energy of the visuals.  That said, it does look like a lot of work went into this.  Keep workshopping the game and the trailer; games are an iterative art form.  There’s no shame in using AI, just keep working towards a better product!

replies.author: TheLuckyOrangutan
replies.body: Cheers for this. It was our first crack at a gameplay trailer, and again, everyone we sent it to loved it, so this outside perspective from people who haven't already played and enjoyed it is very, very helpful.  We're also taking another look at our art direction, so we're pushing our release back to early next year, maybe. Just to make sure everything is strong visually, since that was largely our biggest criticism from this post. Thanks again.

replies.author: TheLuckyOrangutan
replies.body: Thanks for this. When we're playtesting, we're a bit lost in the gameplay and roguelike interactions side, so this outside perspective is very helpful.

replies.author: TheLuckyOrangutan
replies.body: Hey mate, thanks for the feedback on this one. We were honestly a bit surprised by how poorly received the art style was on this post, since our 40 playtesters a) seemed fine with it OR even liked it, and b) never mentioned it and focused on UI / gameplay fixes. Our median play time was 1.5 hours; we felt it was ready to launch soon.  So this was a good reality check, as this was a stylized art direction, and it took about 5 months or so to get this far with many, many subs. We're going to take a strong look at the art and animations now to see how we can improve and step up those visual aspects to achieve a much more palatable aesthetic with the bones we have.

You don't need images it's pixel art Opus 5.5 decent at converting it across. Only part you might have issues with is characters/animations only part all AI models suck at take month Sundays to get solid. Like I think your game is solid idea just the graphics are big let down cause you can tell its chatgpt generating the images and people hate that.

replies.body: Oh cool, will look into that for sure. Currently running a bit of RnD with a tester map and units, and will see what works best as new, improved art direction & workflow. Will defs give this a crack.
